MINUTES OF THE
  LOMITA CITY GOUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, MARCH 15,2022

PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDER N.O8-21 ISSUED BY GOVERNOR NEWSOM AND
A836,I, THE PUBLIC AND COUNCIL PARTICIPATED IN THIS MEETING IN PERSON AND VIA
zooM.

1, OPENING CEREMONIES
  a. Call Meeting to Order
  The regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order by Mayor Segawa at
  6:08 p.m. on Tuesday, March 15,2022.

  b. Flag Salute
  Council Member Uphoff led the salute to the flag.

  c. lnvocation
  Mayor Pro Tem Waite gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

  PRESENT: Council Members: Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa (present in Council Chambers)

  Council Member Gazeley (participated via Zoom)

  ABSENT: None

  STAFF PRESENT: City Manager Smoot and City Attorney Rusin (present in Council
  Chambers)

  Administrative Services Director Kamada, Management Analyst Hernandez,
  Administrative Analyst lbarra, Administrative Analyst Bucklew, and City Clerk Gregory
  (participated via Zoom)

  e. Closed Session Report
  City Attorney Rusin announced that the City Council met in open session at 5:15 p.m. and
  recessed to closed session to discuss the following items:

  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to S 54956.9(dX2): One matter
  Letter received January 18, 2022, from Kevin Shenkman regarding threat of litigation
  under California Voting Rights Act of 2001 .

  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL-ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  lnitiation of litigation pursuant to $ 5a956.9(d)(a): One matter

  All members of the City Council were present. There was no reportable action taken for
  the first item. For the second item the Council voted unanimously to authorize the filing of
  a petition for receivership for property located in the City that has a large number of code
  violations that have not been cured.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA
  Council Member Uphoff made a motion, seconded by Council Member Waronek to approve
  the agenda.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

3. PRESENTATIONS
  None scheduled.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Michael Mackavoy, Lomita Community Library Manager, announced upcoming events and
  programs.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

  Council Member Waronek reported on the following:
  .  March 2-4 - Califo,nia Contract Cities Association Legislative Tour; while in
  Sacramento he attended a press conference at the Capitol Building regarding
  proposed bills relative to catalytic convertors theft and street racing
  .  March 7 - Lunch with L.A. County Sheriff Alex Villanueva and Marcel Rodarte,
  Executive Director of the California Contract Cities Association
  .  March 9 - Kinetca Torrance grand opening

  may be found al www.lomitachamber.orq
  Announced the Golden Apple Awards, Friday, May 6, 2022, at the Torrance
  Doubletree

  Council Member Gazeley reported on the following:
  o March Southern Califomia Association of Govemments meeting
  o March 3 - Southern California Association of Governments transportation committee
  meeting
  . March 10 - L.A. County West Vector Control District meeting

  Council Member Uphoff had nothing to report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Waite reported on the following:
  oMarch 2-4 - California Contract Cities Association Legislative Tour
  oMarch 4 - Funeral for Jim Cole
  .March 14 - South Bay Cities Council of Govemments steering committee

  Mayor Segawa reported on the following:
  o Founders Day planning meeting
  . Meeting with L.A. County Supervisor Janice Hahn

6. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT (information only)
  City Manager Smoot stated that the City is currently accepting applications for several
  positions in Public Works and for two parking enforcement officers.

7. CONSENTAGENDA
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: That Consent Calendar ltems 7 a-n be approved.

  Council Member Uphoff made a motion, seconded by Council Member Gazeley to approve
  the recommended action.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  Approved the following consent calendar items:

  a  Motion to Waive Full Reading of Ordinances and that They be Read in Title Only

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve Motion.

  b. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of February 1,2022, and February 15,2022
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve minutes.

  c. Warrants/Payroll Register
  RECoMMENDED ACTION: Approve and file Warrants/Payroll Register.

  d. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the report.

  e. Monthly Report for the City Manager's Department
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the report.

  f. Monthly Report for the Community and Economic Development Department
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the report.

  g. Monthly Report for the Recreation and Facilities Division
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the report.

  h. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the report.

  i. January 2022 Treasury & lnvestment Report
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file the report.

  j. Virtual City Council Meetings as Well as Virtual Meetings for All Other Cig Commissions
  and Committees Pursuant to AB 361

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Authorize remote teleconference/virtual meetings of all City
  of Lomita legislative bodies, including all City commissions and committees, in accordance
  with Assembly Bill 361 fAB 361"), by finding that: (1) a statewide state of emergency is
  currently in place; (2) state and local officials have imposed or recommended measures
  to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19.

  k. Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 831 Relating to Regulating Campaign
  Contribution Limits

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Ordinance.

  ORDINANCE NO. 831 . AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, ADDING SECTION 2-1.30,1 ..CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION
  LIMITS" TO TITLE 2, CHAPTER .I "ADMINISTRATION" OF THE LOMITA MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO ESTABLISH REGULATIONS AND LIMITATIONS ON CAMPAIGN
  CONTRIBUTIONS FOR CITY ELECTED OFFICIALS

  l. Resolution Extending the City's Emergency Measures
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution.

  RESOLUTION NO. 2022.09. A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND AFFIRMING ACTIONS OF THE
  DIRECTOR OF EMERGENCY SERVICES RELATED TO THE CITY'S EMERGENCY
  MEASURES, AND TAKING RELATED ACTIONS

  m. Agreement with MSW Consultants to Provide SB 1383 Recycling Compliance and
  Reporting Software

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Authorize the City Manager to sign an agreement with MSW
  Consultants to provide SB 1383 Recycling Compliance and Software.

  n. Online Business Licensing and Public Works Permitting Solution Agreement
  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Aulhorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with
  OpenGov lnc. (OpenGov) to provide permitting software set-up, training, implementation
  for a one{ime not lo exceed fee of $20,500; and enter into an agreement for annual
  licensing and maintenance for five years at a cost of $25,000 annually.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS

8. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF A DATE AND TIME FOR THE CIP MASTER
  PLAN STUDY SESSION

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Set the date for CIP Master Plan Study Session review for
  Thursday, April 28, 2022, al4:00 p.m.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council lo set the date for the CIP
  Master Plan study session review for Tuesday, April 26, 2022, at 4:00 p.m.

9. DISCUSS]ON AND CONSTDERATION OF A PUBLIC WORKS AGREEMENT wlTH
  SEQUEL CONTRACTORS, INC. FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF STREET
  RECONSTRUCTION PROJECT - ZONES C & F

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1 ) Approve an amended total project budget of $3,1 92,672.05;
  and 2) Award a Public Works Agreement to Sequel Contractors, lnc. in the amount of
  $2,252,552 for the Construction of Street Reconstruction Pro.iect - Zones C & F; and
  3) Approve a contingency of $337,882.8 (15%); and 4) Authorize the City Manager and City
  Clerk to execute the Public Works Agreement.

  City Manager Smoot presented the staff report as per the agenda material. There was a brief
  discussion by Council relative to the streets covered in the project and project funding. There
  were no requests from the public to speak.

  recommended action.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waronek, Mayor Pro Tem Waite, and Mayor
  Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None scheduled.

10. ADJOURNMENT

  There being no further business to discuss, Mayor Segawa adjourned the meeting at 6:37 pm.
